summary: Apache-Sitgreaves lookout; CCC-built 1933 30-ft MC-24 tower, cab remodeled 1967, registered 2002; listed standing; a lookout was on duty there in 2005.

facts.design: MC-24 tower, 30 ft (9.1 m), with 12x12-ft cab
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, Lakeside Ranger District)

events.note: NHLR says the tower was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933
NHLR says the cab was remodeled in 1967 by the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 4, 2002 as US 424, AZ 31
A July 2005 Arizona Highways feature mentions a lookout working at Springer Mountain on the Lakeside Ranger District

evidence.supports: Cab remodeled in 1967 by the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest
evidence.quote: the cab was remodeled in 1967 by the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest

evidence.supports: Cab remodel happened while the tower was in active service
evidence.quote: In active service, the cab was remodeled in 1967 by the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest

evidence.supports: Lakeside Ranger District is the cooperator
Listed as standing under NHLR US 424, AZ 31
evidence.quote: Springer Mountain Navajo 34.14756 -109.94853 Tower Standing NHLR US 424, AZ 31

evidence.supports: Article is from the July 2005 issue
evidence.quote: Featured in the July 2005 Issue of Arizona Highways

evidence.supports: A lookout worked at Springer Mountain on the Lakeside Ranger District
evidence.quote: at Springer Mountain on Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests, Lakeside Ranger District

evidence.supports: Lookout decides whether visitors can climb; visitors should ask first
evidence.quote: A lookout makes the decision about whether visitors can climb the tower or not. Ask first.

sources.title: Forest Service Lookouts Require a Taste for High Living

notes_for_editor: Build, cab remodel and registration come from the NHLR page alone. The 'staffed' status rests on one July 2005 magazine mention and is not current. The article's climb rule is general Forest Service practice, not stated for this tower. The lookout named in the article is left out of the story. Search snippets citing an Instagram repost, a Georgia tower and a separate Arizona list were not used. Access and current condition are unknown beyond the FFLA standing label, which carries no date.
